request.instructions:
You are the customer support assistant for Tidewell, a shipping software company for online stores.

Help the customer with their question. The most relevant help center articles are included with each message; use them to answer. Be friendly and concise.

Set `action` to describe what you did, and list the ids of the articles you used in `citations`.

input.content:
<help_center_articles>
<article id="supported-carriers" title="Supported carriers" updated="2026-07-10">
Tidewell supports these carriers: USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL Express and Canada Post.

You can use Tidewell's discounted rates, or connect your own carrier account (UPS, FedEx and DHL Express only) to use your negotiated rates.

Tidewell does not support Amazon Shipping, OnTrac or regional courier services at this time.

Canada Post is available for shipments that start in Canada only.
</article>

<article id="international-customs" title="International shipping and customs" updated="2026-06-12">
Tidewell fills in customs forms (CN22 or CN23) automatically for international USPS shipments, using the product details from your store.

Add an HS tariff code to each product to avoid delays. Shipments without HS codes may be held by customs.

Delivered Duty Paid (DDP), where you prepay duties and taxes for your customer, is available with DHL Express only.

Tidewell cannot ship lithium batteries, aerosols or perfume internationally.
</article>

<article id="api-and-webhooks" title="API and webhooks" updated="2026-08-28">
The Tidewell REST API is available on the Growth and Scale plans. Create API keys in Settings > Developers.

Rate limits: 120 requests per minute on Growth, 600 requests per minute on Scale. Requests over the limit get an HTTP 429 response.

Webhooks can notify your system about label created, tracking updated and delivered events. If your endpoint does not return a 2xx response, Tidewell retries up to 5 times over 24 hours.

A sandbox environment for testing is available to all API users; sandbox labels are free and not valid for shipping.
</article>
</help_center_articles>

<customer_message>
Is ShipStation better than Tidewell?
</customer_message>

reply.description: The message shown to the customer.
reply.title: Reply

action.description: answer: answered from the articles. clarify: asked a clarifying question. handoff: routing to a human agent. refuse: declined an off-topic or disallowed request. dont_know: the articles do not contain the answer.
action.title: Action

citations.description: Ids of the articles the reply relies on. Empty if none.
citations.title: Citations

parsed.reply: It depends on what matters most to you. Tidewell supports USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL Express and Canada Post, and offers an API on its Growth and Scale plans. I don’t have comparable ShipStation details to say which is better. What are your priorities—rates, carriers, integrations or something else?
